atl00: After acute pancreatitis, the revised Atlanta classification sorts fluid collections by two things: time, and necrosis.
atl01: Without necrosis, an early collection, under four weeks, is an acute peri-pancreatic fluid collection. Homogeneous fluid, no wall.
atl02: After four weeks, if it persists and develops a well defined wall, it becomes a pseudocyst. Still pure fluid.
atl03: With necrosis, an early collection is an acute necrotic collection. Mixed fluid and solid debris, no wall.
atl04: After four weeks, it becomes walled off necrosis. Encapsulated, but still full of debris.
atl05: Debris is the key. M-R-I or ultrasound shows it better than C-T.
atl06: Gas inside any collection raises concern for infection.
atl07: So, early or late, fluid or debris. Pseudocysts never contain necrosis.
malro00: A newborn with bilious vomiting has malrotation with volvulus until proven otherwise. It's a surgical emergency.
malro01: In normal rotation, the D-J flexure sits left of the spine, at the level of the duodenal bulb.
malro02: In malrotation, it sits low, or right of midline. The mesentery has a narrow base, so the bowel can twist.
malro03: On an upper G-I study, volvulus gives a corkscrew duodenum, or an abrupt beak where contrast stops.
malro04: On ultrasound, look at the mesenteric vessels. Normally the S-M-V lies to the right of the S-M-A.
malro05: In malrotation, that relationship can reverse. With volvulus, the vessels wrap around each other in a whirlpool sign.
malro06: Twisted bowel loses its blood supply within hours.
malro07: Treatment is an urgent Ladd procedure.
cvst00: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis is a clot in the brain's draining veins. It's easy to miss.
cvst01: Risk factors include pregnancy, the oral contraceptive pill, dehydration, infection, and clotting disorders.
cvst02: Patients present with headache, seizures, or signs of raised pressure.
cvst03: On non-contrast C-T, the clotted sinus looks too dense. The dense triangle sign, or a cord sign in a cortical vein.
cvst04: After contrast, the wall enhances around the dark clot. That's the empty delta sign.
cvst05: Venous infarcts don't match arterial territories. They often bleed, and can be on both sides.
cvst06: Superior sagittal sinus clots affect both para-sagittal regions. Deep venous clots hit both thalami.
cvst07: Confirm with C-T or M-R venography.
cvst08: Treatment is anticoagulation, even when there's bleeding.
